title: Ethan Cohen Gallery opens a major retrospective surveying six decades of work by Clark V. Fox
summary: Ethan Cohen Gallery is pleased to present Beyond Obedience, a major solo exhibition surveying nearly six decades of work by Clark V. Fox (born 1946) at the gallery's 251 W 19th Street location in Chelsea. Clark Fox is an American artist whose singular practice defies conventional distinctions between abstraction, Pop art, political painting, and cultural critique. Clark Fox is an artist's artist if there ever was one. At almost 80, his name is known and admired among an interesting group of his elders and peers. As a very young painter, he both emulated and influenced Washington D.C. artists such as Thomas Downing, Gene Davis, Jacob Kainen, and Sam Gilliam. They influenced Clark's early incarnation as a Washington Color School painter. Living his entire life between D.C. and New York, by 1970 the artist had moved from abstract to representational painting. title: Rob Strati finds new possibilities in the broken pieces of the past
summary: At Art Miami 2026, the artist's acclaimed Fragmented series transforms discarded porcelain into intricate imagined worlds, while his smaller-scale works and Service series reveal the breadth of his practice. Rob Strati transforms fragments of antique and vintage porcelain into intricate works of art, drawing beyond the original designs to create scenes that seem to spill off the plate and onto the page. Ships, figures, animals, landscapes and surreal details emerge from the patterns and edges of the broken china, turning what might otherwise be discarded into something unexpected. Through his acclaimed Fragmented series , Strati blurs the line between sculpture, drawing and storytelling. The porcelain isn't repaired or concealed. Its cracks, edges and missing pieces become essential to the finished work, with the original decorative patterns serving as the starting point for an entirely new composition.

title: Chocolate before Columbus: Ancient trade routes from the Maya world to the Mississippi Valley
summary: Long before Columbus, extensive Indigenous trade networks connected the Maya civilizations of Guatemala, Honduras, and Mexico with regions far to the north, including the American Southwest and the Mississippi Valley. These networks carried obsidian, turquoise, copper, marine shells, tropical birds, and ceremonial goods across thousands of miles. Paquimé (Casas Grandes), in Chihuahua, Mexico, was an important northern exchange center, linking communities of northern Mexico with the American Southwest. Farther east, the great Mississippian centers of Cahokia and Etowah participated in equally sophisticated commercial networks. title: Jack B. Yeats masterpieces headline Whyte's November auction in Dublin
summary: Whyte's auction of Important Irish Art promises to deliver another exciting opportunity for collectors to acquire rare artworks of outstanding quality and enduring value. On Monday 23 November 2026 the auction has 147 lots of Important art valued at €1.8 million. 'Am I on the Right Road for the Sea?' (lot 18, €150,000-€200,000) is a late Jack Yeats' painting that questionS the meaning of life - through characters that have become familiar through the years. His maternal grandfather in Sligo ran cargo boats back and forth to Liverpool, on which, at the end of a holiday, the family started their way back to the house in London. Jack, who stayed behind in his formative years, and went to school in Sligo, spent every spare moment on the quays, following the sailors into their homes to hear the gossip. title: Krannert Art Museum opens exhibition exploring contemporary Taiwanese ink painting
summary: A new exhibition at Krannert Art Museum at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign explores how the more than 1,000-year-old tradition of ink painting has recently been shaped and reinterpreted by artists in Taiwan. The exhibition, Ink Shower: Contemporary Taiwanese Artists Reimagine Tradition, was collaboratively produced by Krannert Art Museum, University of Illinois’s Center for East Asian and Pacific Studies, Taiwanese curator Kai-Ching Hsiao, the InART Space gallery in Taiwan, and other advisors and artists. The exhibition opens with a reception on Nov. 5 and is on view through Feb. 27. A wide range of events will accompany the exhibition, including a Center for Advanced Study MillerComm lecture on Nov. 4 by internationally renowned artist Yao Jui-Chung, whose work is in the exhibition, and an artists panel discussion on Nov. 6. title: Sherié Franssen explores memory, emotion, and abstraction in ninth solo show at Dolby Chadwick Gallery
summary: Dolby Chadwick Gallery announced Everything We Carry, an exhibition of new paintings by Sherié Franssen. There is something wonderfully unreliable about memory. A small detail can remain astonishingly clear while everything around it softens. A color, a shape, a feeling can return without warning, sometimes more vivid than the original moment itself. Sherié Franssen’s newest body of work seems to inhabit this space, where impressions gather, shift and resurface, and where what we see is shaped as much by what we bring to it as by what is actually there. These paintings are abundant. Color moves freely across the canvases, sometimes in broad sweeps and elsewhere in quick, concentrated marks. Forms overlap, collide and emerge through layers of paint, occasionally arriving at something that feels strangely familiar before slipping away again. title: Winston Wächter Fine Art opens a new exhibition of paintings by Katherine Bowling
summary: Winston Wächter Fine Art is presenting Forecast, a new series of works by Katherine Bowling. In her second solo exhibition with the gallery, Bowling continues her practice of meditative and luminous paintings. In her newest body of work, each piece suggests habitation and memory, yet often feel strangely distant, like structures encountered in a dream. Bowling’s paintings are inspired by the tradition of the Hudson River School of the 19th century. Utilizing quiet symbolism, Bowling infuses a Romanticist aesthetic into the details of each scene, with the paintings in this series moving between the observed landscape and an interior one. Fields, trees, fences, roads, and solitary houses create places that feel both familiar and slightly elusive. For Bowling, many of these works are inspired by the Hudson Valley area where she lives and memories of her childhood growing up in Virginia. title: Baron de Reuter & Gordon Bennett collection hits the art market
summary: Piguet is unveiling at auction, for the first time, an exceptional collection from the families of the Barons de Reuter and James Gordon Bennett Jr., two names inextricably linked to the history of the international press. Preserved by their descendants for more than a century, works of art, fine jewellery, silverware and precious historical records tell the story of these families, who shaped European history in the late 19th and 20th centuries. Among the major discoveries are two sculptures by Auguste Rodin, including a cast of his iconic Thinker (est. CHF 4 to 7 million, USD 4.9 to 8.6 million, EUR 4.3 to 7.6 million, GBP 3.6 to 6.3 million), as well as an exceptional, unique and previously unseen imperial piece by the house of Fabergé. This extraordinary gift from the Tsar’s family is the largest elephant known to date to have been produced by the workshops of the celebrated goldsmith. title: Christie's Paris announces major design sale celebrating a century of bronze artistry
summary: On 24 November, Christie's Paris will bring together approximately 180 works tracing a century of decorative arts and design. From Alberto and Diego Giacometti to Ingrid Donat and Maarten Baas, by way of François-Xavier and Claude Lalanne, the sale places bronze firmly in the spotlight. By turns decorative, sculptural and functional, bronze remained throughout the twentieth century a remarkable medium for experimentation. Spanning from the Belle Époque to contemporary creation, the works assembled demonstrate the ability of leading creators to continually reinvent this material: sculpture transformed into functional objects by the Giacomettis, the poetic menagerie of the Lalannes, and bronze used as an architectural medium by Ingrid Donat and Maarten Baas. A highlight of the sale, François-Xavier Lalanne's Grand Oiseau de Peter Branché is estimated at €1,000,000-1,500,000. title: Tina Kim Gallery retrospective highlights Kim Tschang-Yeul's 'Recurrence' series and waterdrop motif
summary: Tina Kim Gallery presents Kim Tschang-Yeul: Recurrence, the gallery's third solo exhibition of the Korean émigré painter who devoted five decades of his career to the sustained exploration of luminous, hyperrealistic waterdrops. Focusing on works from the 1980s through the 2010s, the exhibition traces the evolution of Kim’s mature practice as he embraced a more tactile materiality, experimented with varied surfaces and grounds, and began working on a larger scale. At its center is his Recurrence series, which emerged in the mid-1980s, shown alongside significant Waterdrop paintings from across these decades. Together, the works demonstrate the remarkable range Kim drew from a single motif, continually pushing its formal and conceptual possibilities. title: Ouattara Watts blends textiles, global iconography, and jazz improvisation in new exhibition at Karma
summary: Musical notes, eyes, nodes, arrows, numerals, alien vessels, African masks, and modernist sculpture—these are among the vast range of symbols that recur throughout Ouattara Watts’s paintings. His densely layered compositions reflect his omnivorous approach to the histories of painting and visual expression more broadly: a single canvas by the artist, its surface composed of textiles and other materials, may shift between gestural abstraction, color fields, and figuration. Watts’s attention to materiality dates to 1977, when he arrived in Paris to study art from Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire and began painting on tarpaulin. By the time he moved to New York City in 1988, he was already incorporating found objects and fabrics into his compositions. Across New Paintings, Watts sets his enigmatic signs among patterned fabric, papier-mâché relief, and paint-spattered floor cloths, holding the graphic and the gestural in tension. title: Albert Uderzo 'Astérix' pages combine for $579,312 to lead Heritage's $3.1 million International Comic Art auction
summary: A page from Astérix the Legionary depicting Obélix’s awkward first attempt at courting the graceful Falbala charmed the winning bidder to the amount of $206,250 as the top lot at Heritage Auctions’ International Comic Art Signature® Auction, which realized $3,105,825 over two days, Oct. 24–25. The rare page was one of four by Albert Uderzo from his beloved Astérix series, three of which reached six figures, with the comically theatrical original Pilote cover introducing Astérix, Le Devin (Asterix and the Soothsayer) achieving $187,500 and the original painting of Uderzo’s map of France from Astérix le Gaulois realizing $106,250. The production master original art for the image that appeared on all Astérix titles, first published in La Rose et le Glaive in 1991, had its final price set in stone at $57,500. title: MCA Australia and Dia Art Foundation to open a major two-part exhibition of work by d harding in early 2027
summary: In early 2027, the Museum of Contemporary Art Australia (MCA Australia) and Dia Art Foundation present d harding: Inheritance, an exhibition in two parts that are staged simultaneously across hemispheres. The exhibition at MCA Australia is on view from 25 March to 2 August 2027. The exhibition at Dia Chelsea is on view from 19 February to 7 August 2027. Inheritance is accompanied by a co-published monograph, extending the reach of the project to global audiences. d harding’s multidisciplinary art draws on their Bidjara, Ghungalu and Garingbal heritage, unfolding at the nexus of Aboriginal and Western art histories. title: Somerset House hosts 'Through Our Eyes', the UK's first major Sámi art exhibition
summary: This winter, Somerset House presents Through Our Eyes: Sámi Art and Culture, the UK’s first group exhibition to celebrate the arts and culture of Sámi people. The only recognised Indigenous people in Europe, the Sámi’s cultural region (Sápmi) extends north from the middle of Norway and Sweden, and across northern Finland and Russia. Curated by Sámi visual artist Matti Aikio and Somerset House’s Director of Exhibitions Dr Cliff Lauson, Through Our Eyes will showcase the works of 19 Sámi artists across sculpture, installation, photography, video, design, and performance. title: Christie's unveils Hong Kong Luxury Week Autumn 2026
summary: This November, Christie's presents Hong Kong Luxury Week Autumn 2026, marking Christie's 40th Anniversary in Asia and four decades of leadership, innovation, and excellence in the region. Taking place from 18 to 26 November, the season brings together prestigious private collections and iconic masterpieces from around the world, featuring an exceptional selection of magnificent jewels, rare watches, coveted handbags, and fine wines. The auctions are curated by the highest standards of rarity, craftsmanship and provenance, presented through a series of live and online auctions, exhibitions, and special events, offering unparalleled collecting opportunities for clients worldwide while reaffirming Christie's position at the forefront of the global luxury market. title: New partnership unites cultural assets to create premier visual arts research hub in Western Canada
summary: Today, the Vancouver Art Gallery and Emily Carr University of Art + Design (ECU) announced a five-year partnership that will significantly expand public access to one of British Columbia’s most unique research collections. Approximately 5,000 historic artist files will be loaned by the Gallery to the University’s Library + Archives. Spanning nearly a century, from the Gallery’s founding in 1931 to the present day, these files document the rich history of art and artists in British Columbia, while offering insight into artists and practices not extensively documented elsewhere. The files offer an intimate record preserving rare photographs, personal and artistic correspondence, artist statements, exhibition catalogues, newspaper and journal clippings, and other ephemera. title: Rita McBride's 'Arena 3003' hosts live performances and public programs in Lisbon
summary: Pavilhão Julião Sarmento presents Between Continents, a solo exhibition by Iris Buchholz Chocolate. Bringing together two installations shown for the first time in Europe, the exhibition explores connections between Europe and Africa, examining the entanglement of memory, colonialism, migration, and intergenerational cultural transmission. Born in Schorndorf, Germany, in 1974, Buchholz Chocolate has been closely connected to Luanda since 2003, initially through her work with the Luanda Triennial. In A Sul. O Sombreiro (2015), sculptural objects evoke structures of military, secular and ecclesiastical power. The title refers to Pepetela’s novel of the same name, inspired by the colonial conquest of the Benguela region in the seventeenth century. title: Belvedere 21 opens a major international survey of feminist art
summary: The exhibition Feminist Futures Forever at Belvedere 21 brings together 238 international artists from different generations to present a polyphonic, intersectional panorama of feminist art from the historical feminist avant-garde through to possible futures. On view are works by Marina Abramović, Kurdwin Ayub, Kaucyila Brooke, Sophie Calle, VALIE EXPORT, Isa Genzken, Jenny Holzer, Florentina Holzinger, Soli Kiani, Brigitte Kowanz, Barbara Kruger, Maria Lassnig, Kateryna Lysovenko, Ulrike Müller, Yoko Ono, Christiana Perschon, Ulrike Rosenbach, Isa Schieche, Cindy Sherman, Sophia Süßmilch, and Rosemarie Trockel, among others. title: Major exhibition of contemporary Black design unveiled at the Design Museum
summary: Today, the Design Museum in London unveiled an exhibition guest curated by author and journalist Charlene Prempeh that charts the work of some of the most innovative contemporary Black designers working right now. The Nue Black Aesthetic — which opens to the public from this Friday and runs until August 2027 — features 16 designers who are reshaping the design industry. It is one of the most extensive exhibitions on contemporary Black design ever held in the UK. With over 100 objects on display, visitors can see innovative practices that span from fashion and furniture, to architecture, product design and sculpture. title: Richard Long activates Yale Center for British Art's Entrance Court with new site-specific installation
summary: The Yale Center for British Art (YCBA) announced today a commission by internationally renowned artist Richard Long. Gravity is a monumental site-specific installation for the museum’s Entrance Court, inaugurating a year of programming marking the institution’s 50th anniversary in 2027. For Gravity, Long uses his hands to sweep clay across the surface of a freestanding wall measuring twenty-six feet wide by ten feet tall, making a dynamic composition that sets off a dialogue with the iconic flat, steel surfaces of the Louis I. Kahn–designed YCBA building. title: Nara Roesler New York celebrates 50th anniversary with 'The Other', curated by Vik Muniz
summary: Nara Roesler New York presents The Other, an exhibition curated by Vik Muniz that concludes the celebrations marking 50 years of Nara Roesler’s career as a gallerist. On view from November 5, 2026, through January 2027, the exhibition brings together works by Antonio Dias, Julio Le Parc, Tomie Ohtake, Daniel Buren, Richard Long, Sheila Hicks, Heinz Mack, Isaac Julien, JR, Cao Guimarães, Jonathas de Andrade, Amelia Toledo, Carlito Carvalhosa, Marco Maggi, Alexandre Arrechea, Xavier Veilhan, Angelo Venosa, Not Vital, Maria Klabin, Marco A. Castillo, and Jose Dávila, as well as Muniz himself. Bringing together different artistic languages and periods, the exhibition explores how each individual’s perception of themselves depends on an external perspective that remains inaccessible to them: that of the other. title: Jack Shainman Gallery debuts new paintings, drawings, and installations by Donyel Ivy-Royal
summary: Jack Shainman Gallery presents By the time the rain comes, we will be home, an exhibition of new work by Donyel Ivy-Royal, marking his first with the gallery following the announcement of his representation earlier this year. Moving between the familiar and the elusive, the presentation brings together oil paintings, ink drawings, and a large-scale installation. Donyel Ivy-Royal’s practice is shaped by the spaces he has lived in and traversed through, from weathered walls and urban sprawls to trees, mountains, and open landscapes. The sceneries of the Northwest, alongside the underground music, poetry, and art scenes in which Ivy-Royal is deeply immersed, inform the inherently multi-disciplinary nature of his practice.
